title: Validate CSV columns and detect duplicate rows with Python
goal: Check required CSV columns and identify exact duplicate rows before an import.
intro: Inspect modest comma-separated CSV inputs without changing them. This standard-library function checks the header and record width, then reports repeated rows against their first occurrence.
requirements: Decoded CSV text using comma separators.
Pass required column names as a list of strings.
limits: Compares complete rows exactly, including whitespace and letter case.
Does not validate data types or identifier uniqueness.
Accepts decoded text, not a file path; encoding is the caller's responsibility.
Record numbers count CSV records, not physical lines.
Memory grows with distinct rows; use modest inputs.
Header-only input is valid. Additional columns are allowed.
steps: Save the example code as recipe.py.
Import inspect_csv and pass the CSV text and required column names.
Inspect rows and duplicates in the returned dictionary.
Handle ValueError and csv.Error before proceeding with an import.
checks: Seven test methods passed in the pinned Python Docker image.
Covered Unicode, BOM, duplicates, quoted commas and newlines.
Covered header-only input, invalid structure and unclosed quotes.
usage:
from recipe import inspect_csv
result = inspect_csv("id,name
1,Jose
1,Jose
", ["id", "name"])
print(result)
tested_scope: Seven unittest methods passed in an isolated Python 3.12 Docker container with networking disabled. Covers the listed fixtures; does not establish performance for large files or support for every CSV dialect.
